sites.evidence_type: N-terminal HA epitope; parallel surface-display screen
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 298.6 ± 43.2 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by anti-FLAG staining without membrane permeabilization (non-permeabilized condition); receptor reached the cell surface. Signaling and trafficking studies were conducted with the FLAG-tagged construct (L3), implying functional competence, but explicit quantitative comparison to untagged receptor is not reported in the cited clips.
sites.rationale: MC1R is a GPCR with no signal peptide; residue M1 is the mature N-terminus and the entire span 1–42 is extracellular per the topology landmarks, placing an N-terminal prepend (insert_after_residue=0) 42 residues from the first TM boundary (residue 43). No residue number is stated in any ledger line, but for a GPCR with a single extracellular N-terminus and no signal peptide there is exactly one location for an N-terminal tag, so the junction is topology-derived. L2 from the same paper explicitly confirms the FLAG epitope is surface-accessible by non-permeabilized immunostaining, and L3 documents use of the same construct in signaling and trafficking assays. Full-length human MC1R with FLAG fused in-frame to the N-terminus expressed in mammalian cells; anti-FLAG immunostaining performed under non-permeabilized conditions confirmed surface display of the tagged receptor (PMC10532403). The same N-terminal FLAG construct was used in signaling and trafficking studies across WT and RHC variants (PMC4676704). A separate study used N-terminal 3xHA-tagged human MC1R in pcDNA3.1 for receptor characterization (PMC11430673).

sources.claim: In all cases, the flag epitope was fused in frame to the N terminus of the MC1R to yield proteins comparably reacting with a high-affinity antibody.

literature_notes: All ten ledger lines were evaluated. L1, L2, L3, L4, L7 directly support the N-terminal extracellular tag on human MC1R; L6, L9, L10 provide ortholog (chicken, Xenopus) corroboration for the same N-terminal position. The single qualifying extracellular surface site is the N-terminal prepend (insert_after_residue=0). No ledger line reports a tolerated tag insertion in any of the short extracellular loops (ECL1 101–118, ECL2 182–185, ECL3 268–279), so no internal loop sites are proposed. L5 reports cpGFP in ICL3 (intracellular, 212–244) — recorded in other_positions. L6 and L8 report C-terminal FLAG/Myc-DDK tags; the MC1R C-terminus (301–317) is intracellular per the topology landmarks — recorded in other_positions. L8 is a commercial OriGene clone; the C-terminal position is stated but is intracellular. L9/L10 (Xenopus) and L6 (chicken) N-terminal tags are indirect ortholog evidence that reinforces but does not independently create a new site beyond what L1–L4 and L7 already establish for human MC1R.

literature_other_positions.note: cpGFP inserted into ICL3 (residues 212–244, intracellular) of human MC1R to create the FLARE_MC fluorescent sensor; no specific residue stated, representative midpoint residue 228 (Q) used. This is an intracellular insertion, not a surface tag site.
Human MC1R C-terminal Myc-DDK tag (OriGene pCMV6-Entry); the C-terminus (residues 301–317) is intracellular per topology landmarks, so this tag faces the cytoplasm, not the extracellular surface.
Chicken MC1R C-terminal FLAG tag; the GPCR C-terminus is intracellular in all melanocortin receptors, so this ortholog tag is cytoplasmic and not a surface tag site.
